title: Viruses & non-cellular agents
examples: What is the main difference between a virus and a bacterium?
How do viruses reproduce inside a cell?

explain.say: Today we are learning about viruses and viroids. These are tiny biological agents. They are not considered true living organisms. We will explore their unique structures and how they operate.

items: Viroids are even smaller than viruses.
They require a host cell to function.

explain.say: A virus has a very simple structure. It usually contains genetic material and protein. This protein shell around the genetic material is called a capsid. Think of it like a tiny protective box.
Viroids are even simpler than viruses. They are just small, circular pieces of RNA. They do not have a protein coat or capsid. They are much smaller than viruses.
Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites. This means they must live inside a living cell. They cannot reproduce on their own outside a host. They hijack the cell's machinery.
A real-life example is the common cold. The virus enters your respiratory cells. It forces those cells to make more copies of the virus particles. This is how the infection spreads.
A common mistake is thinking viruses are like bacteria. Bacteria can reproduce on their own outside a cell. Viruses need a living host cell to copy themselves.

faq.q: Are viruses alive if they need a host cell to survive?
faq.a: No, they are generally not considered living. They lack the machinery to carry out life processes independently. They are better described as infectious agents.
asks: Do viruses count as living things?
Why are viruses not classified as living organisms?

faq.q: What is the difference between a virus and a viroid?
faq.a: A virus has a protein coat called a capsid surrounding its genetic material. A viroid is much simpler; it is just a small, circular strand of RNA without any protein coat.
asks: What makes a viroid different from a virus?

faq.q: How does a virus take over a cell to make copies of itself?
faq.a: The virus injects its genetic material into the host cell. It then redirects the cell's ribosomes and enzymes to manufacture viral components until the cell bursts.
asks: What process do viruses use to replicate?
Does the virus change the cell's DNA?

faq.q: Can viroids infect animals or only plants?
faq.a: Viroids primarily infect plants. They are known to cause diseases in certain plant species. This is a key difference from many animal viruses.
asks: What kinds of organisms do viroids affect?

faq.q: If viruses are not alive, how do we study them in a lab?
faq.a: Scientists study them by observing their interactions with living cells in a controlled environment. They use techniques to see the genetic material and the assembly process.
asks: How do biologists study non-living pathogens?
What equipment is used to view viruses?

facts: Viruses can contain either DNA or RNA as their genetic material.
Viroids consist only of circular RNA and no protein coat.
Viruses must hijack the metabolic machinery of a host cell to replicate.
The protein shell surrounding viral nucleic acid is called a capsid.

quiz.say: Which agent is composed only of RNA and no protein coat?
quiz.why: Viroids are defined by having only a circular RNA structure without any protein component.

wrong.0: Viruses always have a protein capsid surrounding their genetic material.
wrong.1: Bacteriophages are complex viruses that infect bacteria, meaning they have a protein shell.
wrong.2: Bacteria are living cells and possess their own cellular machinery.

quiz.say: If an agent needs a living cell to reproduce, it is called:
quiz.why: This term precisely describes organisms that must live inside a host cell to multiply.

wrong.1: Autotrophs produce their own food using energy from light or chemicals.
wrong.2: Saprophytes obtain nutrients by decomposing dead organic matter.
wrong.3: Chemotrophs get energy from chemical compounds, not necessarily needing a host.

quiz.say: Which structure is best described as a very small, circular RNA molecule without protein?
quiz.why: This description matches the unique composition of viroids, which are RNA only.

wrong.0: Plasmids are small, circular pieces of DNA found naturally in bacteria.
wrong.2: Viruses always package their RNA or DNA within a protein capsid.
wrong.3: Bacteriophages are complex viruses that infect bacteria.
